hypothesis: The FM currently uses zero user-side features (only user_id, video_id, author_id, tab, duration bucket) — user_features_pure.csv is loaded nowhere in data.py despite being available. Adding a handful of user profile categorical fields (user_active_degree, follow_user_num_range, fans_user_num_range, register_days_range) gives the model generalizable user-side signal that transfers across users, which should especially help ranking for users with sparse train history.
expected_effect: GAUC should move more, since these features let the model generalize across users (improving within-user ranking cases where user_id embedding alone is under-trained), whereas nDCG@5 depends more on item-side signal which is largely unchanged.
